intro:
Zechariah, eleventh of The Twelve (Minor Prophets), contemporary of Haggai, brings eight night visions (ch 1-6) to encourage temple rebuilders. His prophecies are highly symbolic, apocalyptic. Key visions:
1. Horsemen among myrtle trees—God patrols earth
2. Four horns and four craftsmen—nations that scattered Judah judged
3. Measuring line—Jerusalem will overflow with people
4. Joshua the high priest in filthy clothes, Satan accusing—God clothes him in clean garments
5. Gold lampstand and two olive trees—Spirit empowers Zerubbabel and Joshua
6. Flying scroll—curse on thieves and liars
7. Woman in basket—wickedness removed to Babylon
8. Four chariots—God's spirits go throughout earth

Then symbolic crowning of Joshua (ch 6)—merged king/priest role pointing to Messiah.

Second half (ch 9-14): Later prophecies, possibly from different period. Famous passages:
- 'Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! See, your king comes riding on a donkey' (9:9)
- 'Strike the shepherd, sheep scattered' (13:7)
- 'They will look on me, the one they have pierced' (12:10)
- Living water flowing from Jerusalem (14:8)
- Nations coming to worship (14:16)

Zechariah blends immediate encouragement with distant messianic hopes.
outro:
Zechariah is the most quoted Minor Prophet in the Gospels—especially Passion Week prophecies. His visions provide rich symbolic theology: God's sovereignty, cleansing from sin, Spirit's empowerment.

The merging of king and priest roles in chapter 6 points to Christ's dual office. The donkey prophecy fulfilled at Palm Sunday.

Zechariah's apocalyptic style bridges earlier prophets to Daniel and Revelation. His emphasis on Jerusalem's future glory inspires Jewish hope.

Modern reading challenge: Symbolic visions require interpretation but reveal God's cosmic perspective. The book encourages: current obedience connects to God's ultimate kingdom plans.
